PAKISTAN: The persistent denial of adequate health care, family visits, and regular meetings with legal counsel to former Prime Minister Imran Khan and Bushra Bibi, his wife, during their detention is a violation of Pakistan’s international human rights obligations. Imran Khan has not been allowed to meet family since December 2025, barring two meetings with his sister in August 2026, nor has he been allowed to speak to his sons over telephone since March 2026. He has been in solitary confinement, increasingly isolated from human contact, which has impacted his mental and physical health. He is 74 years old and has been experiencing severe blood pressure issues. His family has reported that he has been denied access to independent doctors despite orders issued by the Supreme Court of Pakistan in August that he be taken to a private hospital. His wife is also suffering from an eye condition that could lead to losing her eyesight and has also been denied adequate medical care. 

In denying Imran Khan and Bushra Bibi their rights, the Pakistani authorities run afoul their international law commitments. Article 10 of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, to which Pakistan is a state party, guarantees that any person denied of their liberty "shall be treated with humanity and with respect". 

Imran Khan's family has also been targeted. Three of his sisters were detained on 20 and 21 September and kept under preventive detention under section 3 of the Maintenance of Public Order, 1960 for broad and vague concerns related to planned march to Islamabad by Khan's party Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf. While two of his sisters were released last week, Aleema Khan remains under detention in Kot Lakhpat prison, Lahore. 

Pakistani authorities must immediately provide adequate health care to Imran Khan and Bushra Bibi and restore regular access to family and lawyers. Political persecution of Imran Khan’s family, particularly of his sisters for advocating for his rights, must stop. This includes the immediate release of Aleema Khan, and the authorities must ensure that no further charges are brought against family members for exercising their rights to freedom of expression and peaceful assembly.

author.name: Amnesty International South Asia, Regional Office

The damage caused by Russian ballistic missiles in Ukraine is not just about our losses. It’s not just about making our position in peace talks weaker. It’s also a threat to all of you. Rajon Rondo says the NBA will pay for a player’s college tuition and explains how he used academic bankruptcy to graduate from Kentucky with a 3.5 GPA

“The first two years I was coming out of retirement, I had nothing to do. Kids go to school, now I got a whole 8, 9 hours... So I was like, let me go back and educate myself. I first wanted to learn Spanish because nobody speaks English in Miami. I wanted to go back and my academic advisor been telling me for the last 10 years to go back and I'm like, no, I kept pushing it off. But little do you know, the NBA pays for it. Long as you keep a certain GPA”

“When I left school, back in the day 2004, I dropped out my classes. I left school so I end up failing all my classes, maybe four or five classes. And when you leave school for over two years, you go back and you have a better GPA, which I do have now, all A's and B's, you can file academic bankruptcy. That way those classes that I didn't finish that semester, those fall off my record and now my GPA goes crazy and now I'm going to get me a white cord, graduating with 3.5”
